about.title: About
about.subtitle:
DavIT Futures is my one-person engineering company. You talk to the person who writes the code:
architecture, **backend**, **frontend**, **database**, **CI/CD** and the release itself.
about.name: Dawid Domagała
about.role: Founder · senior full-stack engineer, .NET, web and DevOps
facts: 18+ years in banking, trading, medtech and SaaS
MSc in Electronics, Wrocław University of Technology

items.title: Finance and trading
items.text: Most of my career has been **trading** and **banking** systems: the **L2 Dealer** platform at IG Group, **risk engines** at Credit Suisse, fund distribution for Polish banks. I know what a trader or a risk team expects.

items.title: Quality and security
items.text: Every change runs through **automated tests** and **quality gates** before it merges. I keep the habits of a bank project without its pace.

items.title: DevOps and releases
items.text:
I write the pipelines myself:
**GitLab CI/CD** (17k+ lines at IG), **GitHub Actions**, **Jenkins**, **Docker**. Releases go out without downtime.

items.title: AI agents, human review
items.text: **AI agents** write a lot of my code. I review and test every change before it merges. Agents run only inside your security rules, and your code stays in your repositories.

services.title: Services
services.subtitle: Seven things I do, each with the stack I actually use.

process.title: How we work
process.subtitle: Four steps, no sales layer in between.

steps.title: Direct intro chat
steps.text: Write or call. Tell me about the idea, the system or the problem. You talk to the engineer, not a salesperson.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.text: Scope, estimate and a fixed-price or time-and-materials offer.

steps.title: Short iterations
steps.text: A working demo every one or two weeks, so you can steer early.

steps.title: Release and support
steps.text: CI/CD, docs and handover. Maintenance if you want it.

projects.title: Commercial Projects
projects.subtitle: Nine systems from 18 years, from fund distribution in Polish banks to trading at IG Group.

items.name: L2 Dealer
items.description: **Level 2** desktop trading platform. I rebuilt the delivery process: a **GitLab CI/CD** pipeline of 17k+ lines, **GitFlow** with release branches, **quality gates** and refactors of core modules. The app reached a **HIGH** maturity rating. I also delivered **Price In Size**, part of an IG initiative that made **£15M** in its first month.

items.name: Risk engine platforms: LTV, PRC and PRIIPs
items.description: Migration from **Silverlight** to **Angular 10** with a **GraphQL** backend. Monolith split into **.NET Core** microservices, multithreaded risk calculations, faster **MS SQL** queries and regulatory **KID** documents (PRIIPs) with **BDD** tests across the whole API.
items.outcome: Silverlight → Angular · 100% of the API covered by BDD tests

items.name: QiaCuity and QiaGuest
items.description: UI for a **digital PCR** instrument that counts DNA copies for diagnostics, in **React/Redux** on Linux. Plus **QiaGuest**, a reception app I built from scratch in **Angular** and **.NET Core** on **Azure**.
items.outcome: QiaGuest built from scratch on Azure

items.name: Focis
items.description:
**Multi-tenant SaaS** for law firms. I built it end to end, later with a second developer:
document workflow, dynamic forms, tenant isolation, push notifications and SMS login.

items.name: InCenter and InTire
items.description: Truck fleet management with **tyre-pressure** monitoring. A Wi-Fi router on each truck read the **TPMS** sensors (I wrote the low-level protocol) and sent the data to a server, where a **Vue.js** web app managed the fleet.
items.outcome: 2-week proof of concept that won the contract

items.name: White-label spirometry
items.description: Lung-function diagnostics for clinics and clinical trials, branded for each **pharma partner** under medical-device regulation.

items.name: Elemos
items.description: Software for waste collection: a **WPF** office app and an in-truck app on **Windows Mobile**, later moved to **Xamarin**, with **RFID**, route planning and live vehicle tracking.

items.name: Goniec Online
items.description: Mutual fund distribution system used by many Polish banks: buying and selling fund units and managing distribution networks. Built in **C# .NET** and **MS SQL**.

items.name: DavIT Futures website
items.description: This site: **Blazor WebAssembly** on **.NET 10**, a **three.js** motherboard, two languages, two themes and deploys to **GitHub Pages** on every merge.

games.title: Retro Games Remaster
games.subtitle: Modernizing iconic DOS-era titles to 21st-century standards: native C# (.NET 10) & Avalonia UI and C++20 & Raylib, preserving 100% of original atmosphere and aesthetics while eliminating legacy technological limitations.

civ15.title: Civ 1.5 Remastered
civ15.tagline: Open-source remaster of Civilization 1 (1991, DOS) in C# and Avalonia UI with zero DOSBox needed
civ15.description: The original CIV.EXE binary was translated function by function into clean, high-performance C#. The game preserves 100% of the authentic 1991 retro feel, graphics, and audio, while delivering vital Quality of Life enhancements that players have wanted for decades.
civ15.playInstructionsTitle: How to Play (Zero installation, no DOSBox)
playSteps: Download the latest release for your platform (Windows, Linux, macOS).
Extract the archive and place the original 1991 CIVILIZATION folder next to the Civ_1_5_Remastered.Desktop executable.
Run Civ_1_5_Remastered.Desktop.exe and enjoy silky smooth gameplay with native performance!

games.whatsNewSubtitle: Key gameplay mechanics enhancements and modernization features compared to the 1991 original.

features.title: Units have health & tactical combat rounds
features.description: Units feature hit points (standard 3 HP, veteran 4 HP, elite 5 HP) with health bars on map and in combat. Battles are resolved in tactical rounds losing 1 HP per round rather than a single random dice roll.
features.caption: Tactical combat rounds with unit hit points and health bars (VGA 320x200).

features.title: Load Game directly in the game menu
features.description: Load Game option available directly in the in-game menu without restarting the app. The load list displays both your custom saves and the latest autosaves.
features.caption: Load Game option right in the main GAME menu.

features.title: 20 save slots and 20 turn autosaves
features.description: Save across 20 independent slots (CIVIL0–19) instead of the original 4, plus an automatic rolling pool of 20 autosaves per turn to quickly recover from strategic mistakes.
features.caption: 20 independent slots for manual save games (CIVIL0–CIVIL19).

features.title: Wonders never become obsolete
features.description: Every Wonder of the World retains its full powers for as long as you hold its city, without expiring after modern tech discoveries. Civilopedia reflects all updated rules.
features.caption: Memphis with the Hanging Gardens, providing citizen happiness throughout the entire game.

features.title: Upgrade units for gold in cities
features.description: Upgrade outdated units in cities to their modern equivalents for gold once prerequisite tech is discovered (E key). Upgraded units retain their veteran or elite status.
features.caption: Upgrading militia to phalanx for gold in the orders menu.

features.title: True railroad hubs in cities
features.description: Upon discovering Railroad, every city automatically functions as a full rail hub. Trains no longer lose movement points transiting through metropolises, enabling seamless travel across your empire.
features.caption: Railroad track running continuously through Thebes.

features.title: Fixed 16-bit demographics for large empires
features.description: Fixed 16-bit integer overflow bugs from the DOS original that showed negative approval and production. All demographic indicators in Civ 1.5 are computed with full 32/64-bit precision.
features.caption: A large empire with size 15-22 cities tracked accurately without integer overflow.

australia1859.title: Australia 1859 Sim
australia1859.description: Second project in the remaster series: modernization of a 2005 predator-prey island ecosystem simulator (Borland C++Builder / VCL) to modern C++20 and ultra-lightweight Raylib 5.5, with cross-platform native builds on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

screenshots.title: Island generator, volcanic core
screenshots.caption: The procedural island with terrain noise: beach, grass belt and a black mountain ridge that glows red where the slope is highest.

screenshots.title: Rabbits settle the grassland
screenshots.caption: Early simulation: rabbit colonies spread across the grass around the volcano while the first foxes arrive.

screenshots.title: Foxes and an overgrazed island
screenshots.caption: Later on the rabbits have eaten most of the grass (pale areas) and a pack of foxes hunts them around the big volcano.

australia1859.infoCardDescription: Comprehensive Artificial Life (ALife) ecosystem simulator modeling the historic 1859 Australian rabbit crisis. Vegetation, herbivores, and predators interact in an emergent trophic closed loop on a procedural island. Re-engineered from 2005 Borland C++ to modern C++20 and ultra-lightweight Raylib 5.5 graphics.
